title: Tenant sideband isolation and ballooning controls for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a tenant isolation subsystem that operates as a sideband controller to the scheduler and autoscaler. The feature combines admission-time soft quotas, dynamic ballooning of ephemeral slots, and a headroom leasing mechanism to mitigate noisy tenants and provide predictable throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers.

Background: We’ve observed recurring incidents where a small number of tenants spike synchronous generation workloads and degrade other tenants' P99 latency and throughput. Existing token-bucket quotas and hard slicing are too rigid for some workloads and result in wasted capacity or frequent manual interventions. This ticket proposes a hybrid approach: a lightweight sideband admission controller that negotiates temporary ballooned capacity (short-lived bursts) with explicit headroom and an automated reclaim/soft-quarantine flow when neighbors exceed negotiated behavior.

Goals:
- Reduce cross-tenant tail-latency regressions for Dedicated pools by 50% for median noisy-neighbor events.
- Provide sustained throughput guarantees for customers with reserved contracts while still allowing burstable use for elastic workloads.
- Integrate with autoscaling policies so ballooning respects SLO windows and autoscale budgets.

Non-goals: Do not replace coarse-grained hard-slicing or reserved hard-quotas; this is complementary and intended for mixed workloads on dedicated clusters where strict hard-slices are not purchased by all tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Sideband controller deployed to canary Dedicated pool and negotiates ephemeral balloon leases via admission API
Tenant A (reserved) maintains target throughput within SLA during Tenant B noisy spike in canary tests
Automated reclaim path returns ballooned capacity to pool within configured reclaim timeout and records events in console logs
Metrics show >=50% reduction in cross-tenant P99 latency during synthetic noisy-neighbor tests compared to baseline
E2E tests include both scale-up and scale-down scenarios and a chaos test that simulates node pressure
implementation_steps: Design: define 'balloon lease' protobuf, admission API fields (requested_tokens, headroom_tolerance, lease_ttl)
Runtime: implement sideband controller service that talks to scheduler for tentative slot assignment and to autoscaler for temporary capacity requests
Admission: add preflight check in request path that consults the sideband controller and returns advisory headers (X-Balloon-Accepted/Reason)
Reclaim: implement reclaim workflow with exponential backoff and soft-quarantine state that adjusts token-bucket rates for offending tenants
Console: add ballooning events to Dedicated Console route-level timeline and surface per-tenant balloon metrics
Policy: add a new autoscale-policy flag 'allow_ballooning' and budget accounting so autoscaler can honor lease headroom
Tests: unit tests for controller state transitions, integration tests against canary scheduler, and load tests using workload-generator harness
Docs: Confluence design doc and runbook, and API docs for admission headers and lease configuration
testing_plan: Synthetic noisy-neighbor scenario using two tenants: ramp Tenant B to 5x baseline QPS while Tenant A runs steady load; measure P99 and throughput
Burst acceptance test: request balloon leases of varying TTLs and ensure leases are honored and reclaimed
Chaos: simulate OOM/thermal pressure on a subset of nodes and validate reclaim path and fallback to hard-slice or alternative pool
Long-run soak test over 24 hours to validate fairness windows and autoscaler budget accounting
Regression suite to ensure no increased tail latency for single-tenant Dedicated customers
rollout_plan: Alpha: deploy feature flag gated controller to staging and dedicated canary pool (single region)
Beta: enable for 10% of Dedicated pools with monitoring dashboards and paging on key metrics
GA: enable by default with opt-out for tenants that prefer strict hard-slices; include migration docs
Post-GA: collect two weeks of production telemetry and iterate on reclaim thresholds and headroom defaults
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: controller bugs could incorrectly refuse legitimate leases causing customer throttles; Mitigation: default to fail-open advisory headers and progressive rollouts
Risk: excessive ballooning could exhaust autoscaler budgets and trigger noisy scaling churn; Mitigation: conservative headroom defaults and integrated budget accounting
Risk: subtle interactions with existing token-bucket quotas may create oscillations; Mitigation: add damping and minimum lease TTLs and run cross-team simulation
Risk: observability gaps; Mitigation: add detailed telemetry and sampling of decision traces for first 2 weeks
notes: Related: consult legal for impact on SLAs for reserved customers before GA
